dataflow.name: Simple View images
dataflow.task: Show that Simple View renders a frame that carries images.

nodes.content:
# A frame that carries pictures. The images are inline data: URIs so the node
# runs offline and renders identically on every machine; in a real dataflow the
# column would hold URLs, as the Street Vision pipeline's does.
import geopandas as gpd
from shapely.geometry import Point

ROWS = [
    ("CAoSL1", "vegetation", 31.2, -87.6478, 41.9211, "data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAgAAAAICAIAAABLbSncAAAAEUlEQVR4nGPQO1OIFTEMLQkAZRVaweOB+WcAAAAASUVORK5CYII="),
    ("CAoSL2", "road", 44.8, -87.6402, 41.9265, "data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAgAAAAICAIAAABLbSncAAAAEUlEQVR4nGPwmnATK2IYWhIAWn5swZXi+JcAAAAASUVORK5CYII="),
    ("CAoSL3", "building", 27.5, -87.6351, 41.9302, "data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAgAAAAICAIAAABLbSncAAAAEUlEQVR4nGP4ukwZK2IYWhIAxc1vgZmDLb0AAAAASUVORK5CYII="),
]

gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    [
        {
            "image_id": image_id,
            "image_url": image_url,
            "dominant_class": dominant_class,
            "dominant_pct": dominant_pct,
        }
        for image_id, dominant_class, dominant_pct, lon, lat, image_url in ROWS
    ],
    geometry=[Point(lon, lat) for _, _, _, lon, lat, _ in ROWS],
    crs="EPSG:4326",
)
gdf.metadata = {"name": "street_images"}
return gdf
nodes.goal: Emit a GeoDataFrame whose image_url column holds pictures.
One card per row: the image, then the rest of that row.
